# hands/meme

Teeny's pictures with exact words drawn on, comics, and reaction GIFs.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/meme <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): caption; comic; template
- Job (writes state or calls the core): none
- Operator only (never call): none
- Read only: templates [--query WORDS] [--max N]; gif-search QUERY [--max N]; list [--max N]; get ID

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `caption` | A | stdin `{image, top?, bottom?, style?: "impact"\|"label"\|"subtitle", alt?}`. |
| `comic` | A | stdin `{panels: [{image, caption?}] (2 to 4), layout?: "row"\|"grid"\|"strip", captions?: "under"\|"over", alt?}`. |
| `templates [--query WORDS] [--max N]` | R | Known meme templates from the memegen service: `{templates: [{id, name, lines, overlays, keywords, example}], count, note}`, sorted by id, those whose id, name or keywords hold every word of `--query`, at most N (all; 1 to 300). |
| `template` | A | stdin `{template, lines, teeny?, alt?}`. |
| `gif-search QUERY [--max N]` | R | Giphy search (`GIPHY_API_KEY`, as `x` uses for `gif_id`): `{query, gifs: [{id, title, url, rating}], dropped, note}`, at most N (8; 1 to 25). |
| `list [--max N]` | R | The memes and comics made, newest first, with today's count and the cap. |
| `get ID` | R | One. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `caption`, `comic`, `get`, `gif-search`, `list`, `template`, `templates`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--max`, `--query`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `DRY_RUN=1 hands/meme <verb> --help`. The full account is in docs/hands.md.
